title: An Efficacy Trial of The Toolkit for Optimal Recovery After Concussion
official: An Efficacy Trial of The Toolkit for Optimal Recovery After Concussion
summary: The goal of this study is to test the efficacy of the Toolkit for Optimal Recovery after Concussion (TOR-C), a brief live-video mind-body program. aiming to prevent chronic concussion symptoms and optimize recovery.

interventions.name: Toolkit for Optimal Recovery after Concussion (TOR-C)

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Sustained a concussion 3-10 weeks earlier
2. At least mild anxiety symptoms (score ≥ 5 on GAD-7 anxiety scale)
3. Age 18-35
4. English fluency and literacy
5. Ability and willingness to participate in study procedures, assessments, and intervention
6. Access to a smartphone or computer with internet access
7. Cleared for participation by clinic/study staff

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Participation in mind-body or CBT treatment in the past 3 months
2. Concussion in the past 2 years that resulted in symptoms lasting 3 months or more / current or previous complicated or moderate/severe TBI
3. Practice of mindfulness techniques \> 45 minutes/week in the past 3 months
4. Change in psychotropic medications (e.g., antidepressant, anxiolytics) in the past 6 weeks
5. Uncontrolled bipolar disorder, psychosis, active substance dependence, self reported current active suicidal ideation with plan and/or intent
6. Pregnancy
7. Serious comorbidity expected to worsen in the next 6 months
8. Secondary gains that may bias motivation (e.g., pending disability claim)
